The fix is complete and validated.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `Block::has_value` in `tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs` was a broken implementation. When a receiver consumed the last value of a `BLOCK_CAP` (32)-slot block, `rx.index` advances to exactly the block boundary (e.g. 32) while `head` may still point at the old block (`start_index = 0`). The old code then computed a garbage target offset and matched it against stale ready-bits, returning `true`, which made `Receiver::is_empty()` (tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs:271) report `false` even though `len() == 0`.

**Fix:** Replaced the mangled `has_value` with the correct upstream tokio implementation — a bounds check (`slot_index < start_index` or `slot_index >= start_index + BLOCK_CAP` → `false`) followed by a simple `is_ready` bit check on the slot offset. Out-of-boundary indices now correctly return `false`, letting `is_empty` fall back to the accurate `len(tx) == 0` check.

**Validation:**
- Repro from the issue (bounded & unbounded, 256 send/recv cycles) passes.
- `cargo test -p tokio --features full --tests`: `test_is_empty_32_msgs` (which fails on the pristine tree) now passes; all mpsc suites pass (89 + 28 tests). Only pre-existing environment failures remain (`try_exists`, `connect_v6`, `basic_usage_v6` — identical on the unmodified baseline).
